summary: A 1961 R-6 cab on a 41-foot timber tower in the Fremont National Forest, with earlier 1930s towers and a summer-staffed post.

facts.design: R-6 flat-top cab with catwalk on a 41-foot treated timber tower

events.note: Platform tower established by the Klamath Forest Protective Association half a mile southeast of the summit, per firelookout.com. The register instead places a sawn-timber lookout on the southern point.
37-foot L-4 tower; the register places the first tower on the northern point in 1934 as an L-4 on a trestle-type frame
Current R-6 flat-top cab with catwalk on a 41-foot treated timber tower replaced the 1934 tower

evidence.supports: two summits, Fremont National Forest location
evidence.quote: Located on the Fremont National Forest on the east side of the Cascades in central Oregon, Horse Fly Mountain has two summits.

evidence.supports: original lookout of sawn timbers on the southern point
evidence.quote: The original lookout was located on the southern point. It was constructed of sawn timbers and boards.

evidence.supports: first northern-point tower in 1934, L-4 on trestle
evidence.quote: In 1934 the first tower on the northern point was constructed, an L-4 on a trestle type tower.

evidence.supports: 1961 R-6 cab replaced earlier tower; 41-foot treated timber tower
evidence.quote: In 1961 it was replaced with the current R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 41' treated timber tower.

evidence.supports: placed on standby in the 1970s, later reactivated and staffed
evidence.quote: Placed on standby status in the 1970s, the lookout has been reactivated and staffed in recent years.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
about nine miles south of Bly, Klamath County
1932 platform tower by the Klamath Forest Protective Association, half a mile southeast of summit
evidence.quote: A platform tower was established in 1932 by the Klamath Forest Protective Association 1/2 mile southeast of the summit.

evidence.supports: 1934 37-foot L-4 replaced by present 41-foot R-6 built 1961
evidence.quote: Replacing a 37' L-4 tower from 1934, the present 41' treated timber R-6 tower, built in 1961,

evidence.supports: fuel breaks on roads near the lookout on Bly Ranger District
evidence.quote: establish linear fuel breaks on national forest system roads near the Horsefly Mountain Fire Lookout on Bly Ranger District.

sources.title: Horsefly Lookout Roadside Fuel Breaks
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Fremont-Winema National Forest

corrections.why: The register's own description and firelookout.com both date the current R-6 cab to 1961. Only the register's Built field gives 1960.

notes_for_editor: Early history is disputed. firelookout.com (one source, undated) gives a 1932 platform tower half a mile southeast of the summit; the register places a sawn-timber lookout on the southern point and its first tower on the northern point in 1934. Built field 1960 versus description 1961 (correction proposed). Staffing is undated: the register says 'in recent years' and firelookout.com says 'in the summer'. No public access level, climbing rule or rental listing was found. Staffing as_of left out for lack of a date. The 1970s standby is in the story but has no event entry, because the register gives no year.
